title.en: Many small firms in the long run (Q5)
title.zh: 长期里的完全竞争（第 5 题）

description.en: Cost curves, why free entry pins the price at the bottom of average cost, and how to read an elasticity.
description.zh: 成本曲线，为什么自由进入把价格钉在平均成本最低点，以及怎么读弹性。

description.en: Taking the firm's LMC curve as the long-run industry supply
description.zh: 把单个厂商的 LMC 曲线当成长期行业供给

rows.en: long-run supply: horizontal at $p = 125$ (each firm makes $q = 25$, the bottom of its average cost)
rows.zh: 长期供给：$p = 125$ 处的水平线（每家厂商做 $q = 25$，平均成本的最低点）
$\varepsilon = -4 \times \tfrac{125}{1900} \approx -0.26$：缺乏弹性（市场买 1900，由 76 家厂商供给）

items.en: Average and marginal cost, and why marginal cost cuts average cost at its lowest point.
items.zh: 平均成本和边际成本，以及为什么边际成本在平均成本最低点穿过它。

items.en: A competitive firm takes the price as given and produces where $p = MC$.
items.zh: 竞争厂商把价格当作给定，在 $p = MC$ 处生产。

items.en: Free entry and exit drive profit to zero in the long run: $p = \min AC$.
items.zh: 自由进入和退出让长期利润归零：$p = \min AC$。

items.en: Elasticity: the percentage response of quantity to price, and what it says about spending.
items.zh: 弹性：数量对价格的百分比反应，以及它对总支出意味着什么。

text.en: From total cost $C(q)$ come average cost $AC = C/q$ and marginal cost $MC = C'(q)$. In the **short run** some inputs are fixed (a factory), so cost splits into fixed cost $F$ and variable cost $VC(q)$, with average variable cost $AVC = VC/q$. In the **long run** every input can change, so every cost is variable; Q5's $LRTC$ has no fixed part.
text.zh: 由总成本 $C(q)$ 得到平均成本 $AC = C/q$ 和边际成本 $MC = C'(q)$。**短期**里有些投入是固定的（比如工厂），成本分成固定成本 $F$ 和可变成本 $VC(q)$，平均可变成本 $AVC = VC/q$。**长期**里所有投入都能调整，所以成本全是可变的；第 5 题的 $LRTC$ 没有固定部分。

text.en: Marginal cost cuts average cost exactly at its minimum, because
text.zh: 边际成本恰好在平均成本的最低点穿过它，因为

text.en: so $AC$ falls while $MC < AC$ and rises once $MC > AC$ (a new exam score below your average pulls the average down).
text.zh: 所以 $MC < AC$ 时 $AC$ 下降，$MC > AC$ 时 $AC$ 上升（一次低于平均分的成绩会把平均分拉低）。

alt.en: The U-shaped long-run average cost LRAC = q² − 50q + 750 reaches its minimum of 125 at q = 25, where the rising long-run marginal cost LMC crosses it.
alt.zh: U 形的长期平均成本 LRAC = q² − 50q + 750 在 q = 25 处达到最低 125，上升的长期边际成本 LMC 正好在这里穿过它。

caption.en: Blue: $LRAC$. Orange: $LMC$, which crosses it at its lowest point.
caption.zh: 蓝色：$LRAC$。橙色：$LMC$，在最低点穿过它。

title.en: One small firm: p = MC, and when to shut down
title.zh: 一家小厂商：p = MC，以及什么时候停产

items.en: **Price taker.** One firm among many cannot move the price; selling one more unit brings in exactly $p$. So it keeps producing while $p > MC$ and stops where $p = MC$ (on the rising part of $MC$). Its supply curve is its $MC$ curve.
items.zh: **价格接受者。** 众多厂商中的一家影响不了价格；多卖一个就多收 $p$。所以只要 $p > MC$ 就继续生产，在 $p = MC$ 处停（在 $MC$ 上升的那段）。它的供给曲线就是它的 $MC$ 曲线。

items.en: **Profit** $= (p - AC) \times q$: positive when the price is above average cost at the chosen $q$.
items.zh: **利润** $= (p - AC) \times q$：在所选的 $q$ 处价格高于平均成本时为正。

items.en: **Shutdown (short run).** The fixed cost is paid either way, so the firm keeps producing as long as the price covers average **variable** cost: it shuts down when $p < \min AVC$. Its short-run supply is $MC$ above $\min AVC$.
items.zh: **停产（短期）。** 固定成本反正要付，所以只要价格能覆盖平均**可变**成本就继续生产：$p < \min AVC$ 时停产。短期供给是 $\min AVC$ 以上的那段 $MC$。

items.en: **Exit (long run).** With no fixed costs, a firm leaves when $p < \min AC$.
items.zh: **退出（长期）。** 没有固定成本时，$p < \min AC$ 厂商就离开。

prompt.en: In the short run a firm's price is above its average variable cost but below its average total cost. What should it do?
prompt.zh: 短期里，某厂商的价格高于平均可变成本、但低于平均总成本。它该怎么办？

label.en: Keep producing where $p = MC$: it loses money, but less than if it shut down
label.zh: 继续在 $p = MC$ 处生产：会亏，但比停产亏得少

label.en: Shut down at once: it is making a loss

feedback.en: If it shuts down it still pays the whole fixed cost. Producing covers the variable cost and part of the fixed cost, so the loss is smaller.
feedback.zh: 停产了固定成本照付。继续生产能收回可变成本，还能补一部分固定成本，亏得更少。

label.en: Raise its price to cover average cost
label.zh: 提价到能覆盖平均成本

feedback.en: A competitive firm cannot: at any price above the market price it sells nothing.
feedback.zh: 竞争厂商做不到：价格一高于市场价就一个也卖不出去。

explain.en: Shut down only when the price no longer covers average variable cost. Between $\min AVC$ and $\min AC$ the firm produces at a loss in the short run, and leaves the industry in the long run if the price stays there.
explain.zh: 只有价格连平均可变成本都覆盖不了时才停产。价格在 $\min AVC$ 和 $\min AC$ 之间时，短期里亏着也要生产；如果价格一直这样，长期就退出行业。

title.en: Why the long-run price is the bottom of AC
title.zh: 为什么长期价格是 AC 的最低点

items.en: If $p > AC$, firms make a profit, new firms enter, supply grows and the price falls. If $p < AC$, firms exit and the price rises. In the long run profit is zero: $p = AC$.
items.zh: 若 $p > AC$，有利润，新厂商进来，供给增加，价格下降。若 $p < AC$，有人退出，价格上升。长期利润为零：$p = AC$。

items.en: Each firm also produces where $p = MC$. Both at once, $p = MC = AC$, happens only at the bottom of $AC$.
items.zh: 每家厂商同时在 $p = MC$ 处生产。两者同时成立，$p = MC = AC$，只可能在 $AC$ 的最低点。

items.en: With identical firms, the industry grows by adding firms at that same cost, so the long-run supply curve is **horizontal** at $p = \min AC$ (a "constant-cost industry"). The number of firms is market output over each firm's output.
items.zh: 厂商都一样时，行业扩张靠增加厂商，成本不变，所以长期供给曲线是 $p = \min AC$ 处的一条**水平线**（“成本不变行业”）。厂商数 = 市场产量 ÷ 每家产量。

alt.en: Market diagram. Demand D0 meets the flat long-run supply at A (Q = 1900, p = 125, 76 firms). Demand rises to D1: with 76 firms the short-run supply is steep, so the price jumps to about 199 at B. Profit attracts entry until 92 firms supply 2300 at p = 125 again, at C.
alt.zh: 市场图。需求 D0 与水平的长期供给交于 A（Q = 1900，p = 125，76 家厂商）。需求增加到 D1：76 家厂商的短期供给很陡，价格跳到约 199（B 点）。利润吸引新厂商进入，直到 92 家厂商在 p = 125 供给 2300（C 点）。

caption.en: Demand rises from $D_0$ to $D_1$. **Short run**: the 76 firms move up their $MC$ curves and the price jumps to about 199 ($B$); each earns about 1,900. **Long run**: the profit attracts entry until the price is back at 125 ($C$, 92 firms). The long-run supply $LRS$ is the flat line through $A$ and $C$.
caption.zh: 需求从 $D_0$ 增加到 $D_1$。**短期**：76 家厂商沿各自的 $MC$ 往上走，价格跳到约 199（$B$）；每家赚约 1,900。**长期**：利润吸引新厂商进入，直到价格回到 125（$C$，92 家）。长期供给 $LRS$ 就是过 $A$ 和 $C$ 的那条水平线。

title.zh: 利润为零不等于“没赚钱”

body.en: Economic cost includes the normal return the owners could earn elsewhere, so zero economic profit means the firm earns exactly that return: no more, no less, and so no reason to enter or leave.
body.zh: 经济成本里包括了业主在别处能挣到的正常回报，所以经济利润为零意味着厂商正好挣到这份回报：不多不少，也就没有理由进入或退出。

why.en: Check with the exam's hint: $LMC = LRAC$ at the minimum.
why.zh: 用题目提示检验：最低点处 $LMC = LRAC$。

why.en: For any market quantity: the long-run industry supply curve is horizontal at 125.
why.zh: 不论市场数量多少：长期行业供给曲线是 125 处的水平线。

intro.en: Shortcut from the hint: setting $LMC = AC$, $3q^2 - 100q + 750 = q^2 - 50q + 750$, gives $2q^2 = 50q$, so $q = 25$ directly.

text.en: The (point) price elasticity of demand is the percentage change in quantity per percentage change in price:
text.zh: （点）需求价格弹性 = 价格变 1% 时数量变百分之几：

items.en: On a straight demand line the slope $dQ/dp$ is constant, but $p/Q$ changes, so the elasticity is different at every point: always say **where** you evaluate it. High up the line (high price, few units) demand is elastic; low down it is inelastic.
items.zh: 直线需求上斜率 $dQ/dp$ 不变，但 $p/Q$ 在变，所以每一点的弹性都不同：一定要说清**在哪一点**算。直线上端（价高量少）富有弹性，下端缺乏弹性。

items.en: $|\varepsilon| < 1$: **inelastic** (quantity barely moves). $|\varepsilon| > 1$: **elastic**. $|\varepsilon| = 1$: unit elastic.
items.zh: $|\varepsilon| < 1$：**缺乏弹性**（数量几乎不动）。$|\varepsilon| > 1$：**富有弹性**。$|\varepsilon| = 1$：单位弹性。

items.en: **Spending** $pQ$ rises with the price when demand is inelastic and falls when it is elastic, because $\frac{d(pQ)}{dp} = Q(1 + \varepsilon)$. The same fact gives a monopolist's $MR = p(1 + 1/\varepsilon)$ (next lesson).
items.zh: **总支出** $pQ$：缺乏弹性时随价格上升，富有弹性时随价格下降，因为 $\frac{d(pQ)}{dp} = Q(1 + \varepsilon)$。同一个事实给出垄断者的 $MR = p(1 + 1/\varepsilon)$（下一课）。

items.en: Demand is more elastic with close substitutes, for goods that take a big share of the budget, and over a longer time.
items.zh: 有相近替代品、占预算比重大、时间更长时，需求更有弹性。

items.en: Demand elasticity is negative. Some courses quote its absolute value; write the sign and say which you mean.
items.zh: 需求弹性是负数。有的课本报绝对值；写上符号，并说清楚你用的是哪种。

prompt.en: At $p = 125$ demand is inelastic ($\varepsilon \approx -0.26$). If the price rose by 1%, total spending on the good would…
prompt.zh: $p = 125$ 处需求缺乏弹性（$\varepsilon \approx -0.26$）。价格涨 1%，花在这种商品上的总支出会……

feedback.en: They buy only about 0.26% less while paying 1% more per unit, so they spend more in total.
feedback.zh: 他们只少买约 0.26%，每单位却多付 1%，所以总共花得更多。

explain.en: Spending changes by about $1\% + \varepsilon \times 1\% = 1 - 0.26 = 0.74\%$. Inelastic demand: a higher price raises spending.
explain.zh: 总支出约变 $1\% + \varepsilon \times 1\% = 1 - 0.26 = 0.74\%$。缺乏弹性：涨价让总支出增加。

title.en: Q5b: elasticity at the long-run equilibrium

why.en: The market buys this much at the long-run price.
why.zh: 长期价格下市场买这么多。

why.en: Inelastic: a 1% rise in price cuts quantity by about 0.26%.
why.zh: 缺乏弹性：价格涨 1%，数量只减约 0.26%。

why.en: Not asked, but often next: the number of firms is market output over each firm's output.
why.zh: 没问，但常是下一问：厂商数 = 市场产量 ÷ 每家产量。

prompt.en: How much does the market buy at the long-run price 125?
prompt.zh: 长期价格 125 下市场买多少？

title.en: Traps, and how the question could change
title.zh: 易错点，以及题目可能怎么变

items.en: Giving the firm's $LMC$ as the industry's long-run supply. With free entry the industry curve is flat at $\min AC$.
items.zh: 把厂商的 $LMC$ 当成行业长期供给。有自由进入时，行业供给是 $\min AC$ 处的一条平线。

items.en: Computing the elasticity of **supply** (infinite here, since it is flat) instead of demand.
items.zh: 算成了**供给**弹性（这里是无穷大，因为是平的），而不是需求弹性。

items.en: Mixing $q$ (one firm) and $Q$ (the market).
items.zh: 把 $q$（一家厂商）和 $Q$（整个市场）混在一起。

items.en: **Short run**: the industry supply is the number of firms times each firm's $MC$ above $\min AVC$; a demand shift moves the price (point $B$ in the figure).
items.zh: **问短期**：行业供给 = 厂商数 × 每家在 $\min AVC$ 以上的那段 $MC$；需求变动会改变价格（图中的 $B$ 点）。

items.en: **A per-unit tax $t$ on every firm**: $AC$ shifts up by $t$, so the long-run price rises by exactly $t$ and buyers pay all of it (supply is flat).
items.zh: **对每家厂商每单位征税 $t$**：$AC$ 整体上移 $t$，长期价格正好涨 $t$，全部由买方负担（因为供给是平的）。

items.en: **Demand shifts**: the long-run price stays at $\min AC$; only the number of firms changes.
items.zh: **需求变动**：长期价格仍在 $\min AC$；变的只是厂商数量。

items.en: **Rising input prices as the industry grows** (an increasing-cost industry): the long-run supply slopes up.
items.zh: **行业扩张时投入品变贵**（成本递增行业）：长期供给向上倾斜。

prompt.en: Each firm has $C = q^3 - 20q^2 + 150q$. What is the long-run competitive price?
prompt.zh: 每家厂商 $C = q^3 - 20q^2 + 150q$。长期竞争价格是多少？

prompt.en: Same firms as Q5 (each makes 25 at the bottom of $AC = 125$), but market demand is $Q = 3000 - 4p$. How many firms are there in the long run?
prompt.zh: 厂商和第 5 题一样（每家在 $AC$ 最低点 125 处做 25），但市场需求是 $Q = 3000 - 4p$。长期里有多少家厂商？

explain.en: $Q = 3000 - 4 \times 125 = 2500$, and $2500 / 25 = 100$ firms. The price is still 125: demand changes the number of firms, not the long-run price.
explain.zh: $Q = 3000 - 4 \times 125 = 2500$，$2500 / 25 = 100$ 家。价格仍是 125：需求改变的是厂商数，不是长期价格。

prompt.en: Demand is $Q = 1000 - 5p$. What is the point elasticity at $p = 50$? (Give the signed value, to two decimals.)
prompt.zh: 需求 $Q = 1000 - 5p$。$p = 50$ 处的点弹性是多少？（带符号，保留两位小数。）
